panels.art: Vast darkness with the first faint shapes of the heavens and a formless earth; no figure, no symbol.

text.text: In the beginning, God created the heavens and the earth.

panels.art: A shapeless, barren earth under a starless sky; no life, no landforms.

text.text: The earth was formless and empty.

panels.art: Black, deep water stretching to the edge of sight.

text.text: Darkness was on the surface of the deep

panels.camera: wide, eye level just above water
panels.art: Wind moving across the waters, rippling the surface in long lines. No figure, no dove, no light source (editorial rule for 1:2).

text.text: and God’s Spirit was hovering over the surface of the waters.

pages.layout: large top panel, two bottom panels

panels.art: Light breaks across the darkness over the waters, warm and overwhelming.

text.text: God said,
Let there be light,
and there was light.

panels.art: Light and darkness side by side, a clear boundary between them.

text.text: God saw the light, and saw that it was good. God divided the light from the darkness.

panels.camera: wide horizon, dusk turning to dawn
panels.art: The first evening fading and the first morning rising over the water.

text.text: God called the light “day”, and the darkness he called “night”. There was evening and there was morning, the first day.

panels.art: The waters parting into waters above and waters below, with open space opening between them.

text.text: God said,
Let there be an expanse in the middle of the waters, and let it divide the waters from the waters.

panels.art: A clear sky stretched above the waters, evening light at the edge.

text.text: God called the expanse “sky”. There was evening and there was morning, a second day.

panels.art: Waters drawing back; dry land rising.

text.text: God said,
Let the waters under the sky be gathered together to one place, and let the dry land appear;
and it was so.

panels.art: Bare land meeting wide seas.

text.text: God called the dry land “earth”, and the gathering together of the waters he called “seas”. God saw that it was good.

panels.art: Grass, seed-bearing plants and fruit trees spreading across the land.

text.text: God said,
Let the earth yield grass, herbs yielding seeds, and fruit trees bearing fruit after their kind, with their seeds in it, on the earth;
and it was so.

panels.art: A green, living land at evening.

text.text: There was evening and there was morning, a third day.

pages.layout: tall left panel, two stacked right panels

panels.art: Points of light beginning to appear in the sky.

text.text: God said,
Let there be lights in the expanse of the sky to divide the day from the night;

panels.art: The sun bright over the land, the moon and a field of stars across the night side.

text.text: God made the two great lights: the greater light to rule the day, and the lesser light to rule the night. He also made the stars.

panels.camera: horizon at dusk with moon rising
panels.art: Sun setting and moon rising together.

text.text: There was evening and there was morning, a fourth day.

pages.layout: large panel split sea/sky, small bottom panel

panels.camera: split view above and below the waterline
panels.art: Fish and great sea creatures filling the water below; birds crossing the sky above.

text.text: God said,
Let the waters abound with living creatures, and let birds fly above the earth in the open expanse of the sky.

panels.camera: wide coast at dusk, birds roosting
panels.art: Evening over a sea full of life.

text.text: There was evening and there was morning, a fifth day.

pages.layout: wide top panel, large bottom panel

panels.art: Livestock, creeping things and wild animals across the land.

text.text: God said,
Let the earth produce living creatures after their kind, livestock, creeping things, and animals of the earth after their kind;
and it was so.

panels.camera: low and quiet, golden light on the ground
panels.art: Stillness: the animals at rest, warm light falling on the earth; no human figure yet.

text.text: God said,
Let’s make man in our image, after our likeness.

pages.layout: large top panel, two bottom panels

panels.camera: head-and-shoulders, two figures side by side in warm light
panels.art: The first man and woman side by side, framed from the collarbone up, green leaves softly blurred in the foreground, Eve's long hair falling forward over her shoulders (framing rule Gen 2:25).

text.text: God created man in his own image. In God’s image he created him; male and female he created them.

panels.camera: medium-wide from behind, figures small against a vast land
panels.art: The two seen from behind, small in the distance, standing in tall meadow grass that rises to their shoulders, looking out over the living earth.

text.text: God blessed them. God said to them,
Be fruitful, multiply, fill the earth, and subdue it.

panels.camera: extreme wide, the whole created world at sunset
panels.art: Land, sea, sky and creatures together.

text.text: God saw everything that he had made, and, behold, it was very good. There was evening and there was morning, a sixth day.

panels.art: The finished world under clear sky, from heavens to sea.

text.text: The heavens, the earth, and all their vast array were finished.

panels.art: Calm and stillness across the land; no movement, no figure.

text.text: On the seventh day God finished his work which he had done; and he rested on the seventh day from all his work which he had done.

panels.art: The seventh-day morning in gentle light over everything made.

text.text: God blessed the seventh day, and made it holy, because he rested in it from all his work of creation which he had done.

moral.heading: What This Story Teaches
moral.paragraph: Genesis begins by telling us who made everything: “In the beginning, God created the heavens and the earth” (Genesis 1:1). Again and again God speaks, and what he says happens. The Bible says the same thing later: “For he spoke, and it was done” (Psalm 33:9), and “By faith we understand that the universe has been framed by the word of God” (Hebrews 11:3). Each day God looked at what he had made and saw that it was good, and at the end, “it was very good” (Genesis 1:31). People were made in a special way: “In God’s image he created him” (Genesis 1:27). When God rested on the seventh day, he blessed it and made it holy, a pattern the Bible later gives to his people (Exodus 20:11). Psalm 19:1 puts it simply: “The heavens declare the glory of God.”

quotes.text: In the beginning, God created the heavens and the earth
For he spoke, and it was done
By faith we understand that the universe has been framed by the word of God
In God’s image he created him
The heavens declare the glory of God.
